title: Strive on
hookLine: the Buddha's last words: all component things decay; work on with diligence
carry: decay is inherent in all component things

lines: A GROVE AT NIGHT, TWO SAL TREES.
cards: Last words get repeated. People write them down, argue over them, carve them on stones.
The long discourse on the Buddha's final days ends with his, spoken at night in a grove near a small town called Kusinara, as he lies between two sal trees with his monks gathered close.
Earlier, Ananda has gone aside to weep. The last words are not a blessing, not a promise, not a farewell. They are a short sentence of instruction, half fact and half job.

teach.h: THE TEACHING WILL BE YOUR TEACHER.
teach.b: First, no new teacher. Before the end, the Buddha tells Ananda that some may think: the word of the Master is over, we have no teacher anymore. Not so.
The teaching and the discipline he has given them will be their teacher after he is gone.
Second, any doubts? He asks the monks whether any of them has a doubt or a question about the Buddha, the teaching, the path or the order.
Ask now, he says, so you won't regret later that you didn't ask while the teacher was face to face with you. They are silent. He asks a second time, and a third.
Silence. Third, the fact. Then the last words.

teach.h: DECAY IS INHERENT IN ALL COMPONENT THINGS.
teach.b: Rhys Davids's old translation: "Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!" The first half is the fact.
Everything put together comes apart: bodies, plans, friendships, mountains, the teacher lying in front of them. Nothing in the sentence softens that. Fourth, the job.
The second half doesn't say: so despair. It says: so work.

teach.h: WORK OUT YOUR SALVATION WITH DILIGENCE.
teach.b: The Pali word Rhys Davids renders as diligence is appamada, the heedfulness the Buddha praised in the monks who recalled death with each breath.
Other translators put the line more simply: strive on, with heedfulness. Death is not the end of the sentence. Diligence is.
In this telling, remembering that things fall apart is a reason to use well the time they hold together.

how: Some Buddhists remember the Buddha's last words, recited in Pali, as a reminder of impermanence and a call to practice with heedfulness rather than delay.

o: a call to fight hard against old age and sickness
the Buddha's farewell blessing to his weeping monks
the Buddha's last word: things decay, so keep at it heedfully

games.q: the Buddha's last night — tap the pairs.
p: the teaching will be the teacher
asked three times, met with silence

s: the Buddha's last words were a promise of reward
they were a fact and a job: decay is inherent in all component things; work on with diligence.
before the end he asked the monks three times if any had a doubt
he named a successor to lead after him
he told them the teaching and discipline would be their teacher.

games.q: you are the Buddha, near the end, monks around you. what do you say last?
o: a word of comfort: don't be sad.
a fact and a task: things decay, so work with diligence.
the name of the one who will lead you now.
games.why: he names the fact and hands on the work: decay is inherent in all component things; work out your salvation with diligence.

practice: Bring to mind one small thing in your life that's half done, a message, a drawer, a form, a repair, and notice without scolding why it's been waiting: tiredness, dread, distraction.
Then hold the first half of the line, everything put together comes apart, and let it make the moment feel a little more precious than urgent.

wordCard.voice: Strive on: the Buddha's last instruction. All put-together things decay, so work on with diligence and heedfulness. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali, written in Devanagari: appamāda, heedfulness or diligence, the key word of the last sentence.

carryVoice: Your line: decay is inherent in all component things. The fact first, then the work. Day seven hundred sixty-six.

sources.work: Buddhist Suttas (Sacred Books of the East 11)
sources.q: Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!
